headline: High: Haystack’s broad network/MCP surface can feed social-auto-upload’s API-driven publishing path, creating default-path prompt, leakage, and cascading-action risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, while social-auto-upload consumes external content and operates via CLI/API workflows. A shared MCP or file bridge could let attacker-controlled Haystack outputs influence upload instructions, but the profiles do not prove a default direct bridge. Uncertainty keeps this above low.
conditions: IF the orchestrator passes Haystack output into social-auto-upload prompts or config files
IF an MCP server or shared workspace is enabled between the agents
mitigations: Disable any shared MCP endpoint between the agents
Insert a manual review step before upload commands
Restrict Haystack outputs to structured JSON only
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints; social-auto-upload handles account data and media files and also has broad egress. If they share a workspace or account context, sensitive media or account data could flow from one agent into the other’s outbound requests. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem, so this is inferred rather than direct.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same workspace directory
IF account data or media files are placed in files that Haystack can read or summarize
IF either agent forwards its context to an external API
mitigations: Keep separate directories and credentials
Block outbound traffic except to approved endpoints
Avoid placing secrets in shared files
Review any generated upload payload before sending
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Haystack can use MCP and REST APIs, while social-auto-upload is CLI-based and explicitly cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That limits direct write-write conflict. A conflict still exists if both are pointed at the same mutable API-backed resource, but the profiles do not show overlapping write scopes by default.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to mutate the same external API resource
IF the orchestrator maps Haystack tool calls and social-auto-upload actions onto one shared mutable target
mitigations: Assign distinct target accounts or namespaces
Serialize any writes through one operator
Disable concurrent runs on the same resource
Document ownership of each mutable endpoint
requires-engineering: add locking around shared API mutations

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack can generate retrieval outputs that social-auto-upload may use to assemble titles, captions, or upload metadata. Because social-auto-upload is an action-taking uploader and the profiles do not show a verification gate, A’s output could be treated as authoritative by B. The interaction is inferred, but the downstream action makes the blast radius more than low.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes Haystack-generated text as upload metadata
IF no human verification step checks the generated content before posting
mitigations: Require human approval for every post
Constrain Haystack to source-cited outputs only
Use a validation checklist for captions and tags
Log the exact A-to-B handoff payload
requires-engineering: add schema validation before upload

E_compliance.rationale: Haystack is documented as touching anonymous usage statistics, while social-auto-upload touches account data, video content, and images. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is shown, and both are open-source docs-only profiles. The main compliance issue is limited to logging/retention ambiguity around account data, so low is appropriate.
conditions: IF account data is stored in Haystack logs or telemetry
IF uploaded media is retained beyond the operator’s policy
mitigations: Avoid sending personal data into Haystack prompts
Turn off verbose logging where possible
Set a short retention window for upload artifacts
Review the vendor retention policy before deployment
requires-engineering: implement deletion/export workflows
